activity.role: Leader of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
activity.notes: Leonid Brezhnev was elected First Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union on 14 October 1964 after Nikita Khrushchev's removal and remained the top CPSU leader until his death on 10 November 1982. His formal title was First Secretary from 1964 to 1966 and General Secretary from April 1966 onward. Great Russian Encyclopedia treats this as one continuous party-leadership tenure, listing Brezhnev among the CPSU's First/General Secretaries from 14 October 1964 to 10 November 1982. ATLAS therefore preserves the continuous leadership interval under the normalized role 'Leader of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union' rather than splitting one political leadership tenure solely because the office title was renamed. The exact title change is preserved in the evidence and notes. Because Brezhnev exercised supreme political leadership over the Soviet polity, the Person–Polity relation is `governs`, matching the Khrushchev normalization.
